title: Cardinals Cover 2: A.Q. Shipley Reacts To Michael Wilson Contract Extension | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: How about we just start off the topic, Q? Your initial reaction, the deal gets done. Michael Wilson and the Arizona Cardinals now together, three more seasons through 2029. >> Yeah, it's a it's a massive news. I mean, the minute I saw that come across and all my and my phone started going off with all the notifications that Cardinals and him reached an agreement. I mean, it was huge because what he did the last 10-ish weeks of last season and then obviously what he means to this team. You can tell the locker room loves him. You can tell Jacoby loves him. You can tell the rest of the guys on the team loves him, right? So, I think with with them locking him up before the season starts, now he can just go out and play, right? Like he doesn't have to sit there and worry about going into free agency. I mean, I thought um you know, the way that they've been kind of approaching this, they've locked up Jacoby, they've locked up Froholdt, and they've locked up him now. I mean, that's three cornerstones going into this year's offense that now these guys can just go out and play fast. >> Piggybacking off that, A.Q., you look at the rest of the skill positions, Trey signed through '29, Michael signed through '29, Jeremiah Love signed through '29, and you've got Marvin under contract through 2028. Fifth-year option, all of a sudden he's signed through 2029. So, again, your core special or your core skill players here are together for a little while. >> And that's huge. And obviously, there's still a massive piece looming. You've still got to lock up, you know, the left tackle, right? Paris Johnson's um obviously coming into where he's going to start looking for a contract, right? But I think starting with Fro and then you get the all all the skill guys locked up, that's huge. Obviously, with the rookie contract with Jeremiah Love and what he's I mean, this is a very, very talented skill position group on paper and I think you keep them together for a couple of years and you continue to build around that. Obviously, you know, this this team has a lot to look forward to with a new head coach, right? And a new offense. I think there's a lot of people, especially in the Arizona area, that are really looking forward to see what this team can do. And I'm I mean, I'm more than more than excited to sit there and watch this first game, just to see what the ones can do. I think that's the most exciting part. We've watched, you know, the second team, the third team, and the fourth team go out and do what they've done, and it's been impressive with this offense. We really haven't seen the ones, so I'm excited to see this group get out there and put this new offense to the test. >> The news of the extension is something that Mike LaFleur was asked about the message that it sends to those players in the locker room. You've been in that locker room when a player gets that extension, especially a player who was drafted, drafted, developed, resigned. What kind of message does that send to those players? >> Well, that's huge, and that that's one of the things that I was kind of hoping would get done before the season start. I was I was hoping it got done back in March, honestly. I mean, you saw what he what he did last year, and I was like, "Ooh. I mean, this is a guy that, you know, you can probably lock him up right now and feel really good about a deal for both sides. Both sides would sit here and say, "Okay, this is great." He's going to say it's great. The team's going to say it's great. But, to go back on what you just said about the locker room, the guys see that. The guys know that, and I think that's what's huge, especially, again, like, you know, all in the last couple of weeks, you see what they've done with Fro. That guy is super well respected in the locker room. The guys see that. Now, you reward a guy who does everything right, who is the anchor of your offensive line, and does all that stuff. You see that happen, and then a couple weeks later, you see Michael Wilson, who's been nothing but a fantastic teammate since day one, kind of you know, doesn't have a monster start to the season last year, only like 50-something yards for the first 5 weeks, but he's blocking, he's doing all the things right. Then, all of a sudden, he gets his opportunity, he takes advantage of it, puts the numbers that he did on paper, obviously, in games, and you don't hear him gripe about anything the entire off season. You don't hear him say anything during training camp, right? Obviously, these negotiations have been going on for a while. He wants it, and so to see him rewarded, it speaks volumes to the guys in the locker room, and they see that. Trust me, they recognize it. There's no question about that. >> In addition to the production, what Michael Wilson does in the run game? Something I think he takes pride in, and Michael LaFleur has mentioned that if you're a wide receiver in this offense, you had better block. If you're not, you're not going to get targeted. What have you seen from Michael Wilson in that aspect of his game? >> I mean, that was the first thing I noticed when I came to practice, right? I come back I come back off the summer vacation. I show up at practice whenever we announced JP as the as the play-by-play, and I show up, and I just stuck around. I just wanted to see what this new offense looked like, what it was all about, and um how how they were going to deploy all of all of these weapons, the receivers, all those things. First period I watched, he's motioning down and digging out a safety. Next one, he's coming down and cracking on a linebacker. I'm like, "Oh, okay. This is uh this is going to be expected, and this is what they are going to need, and they are going to want from the receiver position, and we continuously hear it. If you want the ball, you better block. >> What is your expectation for Michael within this offense? Obviously, right now we don't know much except for what we've heard from the head coach, and he keeps bringing up Puka Nacua as far as get that that guy maybe that is responsible for a lot of yards between the 20s, and then certainly a playmaker inside the red zone. But, is that a Is that Is that fair, at least based off what we have to go on for right now? >> I mean, listen, it's it's an easy comparison, right? Because they they were the two most productive receivers on their team. Um obviously, him coming from LA, right? Like I think you can also look at you know, what they've done in San Francisco, right? Jauan Jennings, right? Like what he was able to do. Aiyuk whenever he was healthy, right? Like all those guys, they are all about going down and making the plays, making the plays over the middle, catching the out routes, catching the deep balls, um catching the over routes again on the play action pass, doing all those things. But guess what? What also shows up is what they're able to do in the run game. I don't think you're going to sit there and see um Puka in the Rams system or Michael Wilson in this system be what Cooper Kupp was or be what Jauan Jennings was, per se. I mean, those guys were almost asked to be a blocker first and then a receiver second. I think these guys are obviously, you know, especially [snorts] with Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison, those guys are going to be asked, "Hey, listen, you're you're going to go get your yards, right?" But there are going to be certain instances and plays, especially when we're running the football, especially when we get into a grimy game and we're running a lot of downhill duos or even if it's the outside zone scheme, and it's not going to be asked to do much in terms of that. You're not going to have to sit there and be a fullback, per se, but you are going to have to stick your head in there and you are going to have to get dirty every once in a while. >> You mentioned we haven't seen the first team offense for very many snaps. It did look good when that series that they were out there. What can you take away from that particular series, understanding that you're not game planning, defenses are very vanilla, offenses are very vanilla, but can you read into anything from that particular play, that particular series carrying over into the regular season? >> Yeah, I thought it looked really good. I mean, honestly, I mean, against against the Raiders, they go out and they do what they're supposed to do, right? But again, the thing that I take away from that, more so than just them putting points on the board, was the fact that they got put in a third down situation, right? And they end up converting the first down. It was a penalty, right? But then there was another one where, you know, they hit, I think it was Michael Wilson maybe on an out route, and they end up hitting him on the right sideline, and you know, you're you're you're putting some different situations. That's the biggest thing that you cannot uh simulate, I guess, in practice. I think that's the biggest thing. So, when I look at the preseason, I don't necessarily look at how well they did, right? Like I'm looking at how they handled situations because the NFL's all about situational football. It's how you're handling third down. It's how you're how you're going to handle short yardage and goal line. And they went down and they did exactly that. They got inside the 10. Jacoby makes a heck of a play and they hit Marvin Harrison in the back of the end zone. They got everybody involved, right? I think that was huge. You get Marvin involved, you know, Trey only played one play so he really didn't, but you know he's going to be involved. And then Michael Wilson, he gets a couple catches, looks exactly like he did last year. And then Jeremiah Love wasn't uh fully, you know, what he showed the rest of that game with the first team offense, but then you got to see once he settled in who he's going to be, right? And I think you mix that with Al-G you mix that with Trey and the boys. And then oh oh by the way, like you mentioned, there really wasn't any game planning. There was no game planning for this. This was base offense and it just looked sharp. I thought everybody looked sharp and I think you can take a lot away from that. >> Enough footballs to go around to keep everyone happy this season? >> I think so. I mean I I think the Rams and the Niners have kept everybody happy and they've continued to keep their guys happy, right? I mean you look at you look at all the guys that they've had over the years. I mean you got Davante Adams, you got, you know, the tight ends obviously in the Rams, you got Puka, all those guys are Kyren Williams gets plenty of touches. They got a backup running back and Korm. I mean these guys are all happy. You look at the Niners with Usecheck and McCaffrey and when they had Aiyuk and then Jauan Jennings and now they now they're adding Mike Evans and Christian Kirk, right? Like they got plenty of guys. They all seem to stay happy and you know what makes you know what makes everybody happy, Craig? >> Wins? >> Winning. >> Yeah. >> Winning football games, right? So, I think uh you definitely don't hear as much when you're winning football games. It's a lot more fun to win, right? And I think it's a lot more fun to win when everybody's involved as well and you all feel a part of the offense. >> Let's hope that starts next week. AQ, enjoy the final {quote} free weekend before we really hit put the pedal to the metal, if you will, for this 2026 regular season. >> I can't wait. I'll tell you what Craig. I mean we've we've watched enough of the preseason football. We haven't got to see you know, any of our bell cows really take it. I'm excited to see the bell cows get out there and and do do what they're supposed to do with this first team offense.

title: Exclusive Interview with Derek Barnett
text: Welcome back to Cleveland Browns Daily brought to you by Bally Beneficial Sports Betting Partner of your Cleveland Browns. Very happy to be joined now by the newest member of your Cleveland Browns defensive end Derek Barnett. And Derek, first of all, welcome to Cleveland. Welcome to the Browns. >> Thank you for having me. >> So, this is a situation where you got to choose. I know you had multiple suitors, teams that were interested in you. And here you are with the Cleveland Browns. What was it about this opportunity that made you say, "Yeah, I want to come back. I want to keep playing and I want to do it as a Cleveland Brown." >> Yeah, I definitely wanted to get to 10 years. And I just felt like it was a great opportunity. Um a lot of young guys on this team. A great defense. Uh great great young guys on offense. So, it was just a situation I can come in and and just try to put my best foot forward and help this team. >> You also have a little familiarity with Jacques Cesaire when you were down in Houston, now the defensive line coach. What's it been like to reunite with him? And was that, you know, something that gave you a little more comfort than going somewhere maybe you didn't know somebody like that? >> Yeah, for sure. Uh coming here back with Jacques uh gave me some uh gave me like a little comfort level. Also with uh Malik Collins. Yeah, of course. Um even some some of the coaches I've crossed paths with being in the league for a while. Same with nutrition staff. So, uh if you're in the league for a long time you cross paths with a lot of people. So, it's it's cool like just bumping into people that you've worked with in the past. >> Yeah, when you kind of came in and and got going and kind of saw the room, you know, you have an opportunity certainly in your room with the defensive ends. You are the veteran. You are the one that is that's played at the highest level here in this league. You're the one that's seen, you know, good football, playoff football, championship football. What's it like kind of having that role transitioning with a lot of good young players? >> Yeah, it's cool. It goes by quick. Like you come in as a as a young guy you you're a rook and then before you know it you're a vet. And then uh you know, you just try to you know, give to game back and help the young guys. But you also you can learn a lot from the young guys. There's a lot of great young guys in the defensive line room and I'm learning from them. I'm picking their brains. And and if I can do the same for them, I I I hope to do I hope to do so. >> You love to rush the passer. You still can rush passer at least five sacks each of the last two seasons. What's kind of been the secret to that success and the longevity of it? >> Yeah, I think uh there ain't really no secret. It's It's working on your technique and fundamentals every day. You know, some days may be tougher than others and you're still just just going out there and doing your job, your your assignment and having a good alignment and also just taking care of your body. Make sure you feel good on game day cuz I think everybody in this league is talented and it just comes down to who's feeling the best on game day, you know? >> In Houston, you were also kind of what they call like an attack front defense. Coming here, attack front defense, so that was that some familiarity that made it a little more comfortable? >> Yeah, for sure. That's definitely uh I wanted to go to a team with the similar similar front mindset. Uh you know, saying that attack defense. Um so that that definitely was one of the biggest things for me to come come in uh to Cleveland. >> What's something that you want Browns fans to know about Derek Barnett? Now that they get to see you, we've heard about you. Obviously a first round pick in this league. People know who you are. You've had a lot of success. What do you want Browns fans to think about? Doesn't have to be football related, by the way. Just anything when they see, you know, Barnett on the back of your jersey and you're out there playing for the Cleveland Browns. >> Uh I think they should know I'm going to give my all and give give my best effort, you know? Um and I think that that we owe that to the fans, you know? Um and even just playing in this league, you owe that for the guys that came before us um way before us, you know what I'm saying? So just going out there and playing your heart out. >> How you feeling physically? Nice to not maybe have such a long training camp, but to get in here and still get ready. Got a couple of weeks still before the season opener. How you feeling physically and and being ready to go? >> Yeah, I'm feeling good, you know? It's It's still a daily grind. You just still trying to get better each and every day. Um you know, you don't necessarily feel 100%. I mean, probably not until >> [laughter] >> you're you're coming out of college, you know what I'm saying? So uh you know, it's still just getting better each day and getting my conditioning right and just getting my hands and my technique and my get off right. So uh you know, we once not here until we still got some time, so you're still sharpening your tools and and getting ready to go out there and play ball. >> And you got familiar face, Titus Howard, across from you. You got it. I'm sure you've gotten there and you guys can work together and and keep beating each other better. Iron sharpening iron. >> Absolutely. >> Absolutely. Well, Derek, it's great to have you here. Welcome to the Browns. Can't wait to see you out there, and uh let's go, man. Couple weeks and and get after it. >> Oh, yeah. Thank you for having me. >> All right, you got it. Derek Barnett, our guest here. We'll be back with more Cleveland Browns Daily, brought to you by Bally Bet, right after this.

I mean, is there something about them that we think can help us uh this year and moving forward? Uh we'll see if he practices today. He wasn't out there yesterday. Um, biggest thing is trying to be able to keep him because he's reckless with his body, plays with that abandonment that you want. Trying to keep him healthy is the biggest thing because when he's out there, he is very disruptive. He is a a huge plus for us defensively. >> So with Harold, how is he like the tight ends you've coached in the past? How is he different from those guys? >> Um Harold is still a developmental blocker, but what I do like about him is guys at times with his athleticism aren't all in on the the blocking aspect of it, which he has shown he will be. he will do that for our team and so that's still a work in progress. Um we certainly there was parts of the spring we didn't have him. So but I think he has the ability to be a matchup player but also an elite run after catch guy. What I've seen on film is the run after catch and a bull with a ball in his hands. Now it's can we get him >> in terms of his development further along in his blocking and then as a matchup player. How did Austin unless there's an injury concern? >> I just think we saw a lot of upside to the player, maybe not the consistency uh at this point in his career, but I think there's enough there to uh at least warrant keeping him around and then see where it goes from there. Did Austin, how did Austin look in his I think it was probably his first time working with the ones right out. How did he fit in? >> He's fine. He was fine. I mean, he's only going to continue to get better. He's still a young player. Uh working his way through the bumps and bruises and the offense and whatnot, but uh he was fine. >> For a guy that big is >> Sure. >> Sure. Yeah. No, he's he's only going to continue to get better and we're only going to know. I mean, again, their defensive style is completely different than ours. So, to try and compare uh attack style jet up the field compared to knockback style, bigger bodies, uh we'll only know when we play. For a guy that big, is there any question when he moves inside whether or not he can get low enough, you know, season? >> No, I mean, again, I think it remains to be seen once we play a different style. And and I I like the way he's wired, the way he works. Nothing about what he has shown thus far tells me that he is not capable of executing what we're going to ask him to do at guard or at tackle. depends on making sure the starters stay healthy, don't play them often in the preseason. So my question is, is there a downside to that as you go into the >> Sure there is. I think where is that sweet spot of how many days of pads you have on, right? How many uh reps do you take uh where there's contact involved, right? I mean, but where's the upside of getting the reps against good people? That's a development piece, right? Where is that balance of development with the potential for injury, right? Right. I mean, that's just the way it is, right? I mean, as you're moving forward with anything in life, it's Right. There's benefits to both, right? You can't just walk through all the time and you can't beat the heck out of your guys and playing all the preseason games. So, we thought we struck a pretty good balance there and uh with our guys and I think and they haven't shown any propensity to not want to hit and not and not enjoy contact. >> That's part of it. I mean, it's uh it's again, it's it kind of falls back in the same question is that how much do you want to expose your quarterbacks to the hits and uh and yet where can you take advantage of certain situations that helps you offensively? So, we'll have to weigh that risk as we move forward. when you look back in >> um in the two years previous to last year when I was there, I don't remember him being significantly hurt, run or pass. Now, he is really elusive. He is has an uncanny ability to avoid direct hits. Never seen anything like it. His spatial awareness, which shows up in the passing game, is the same in the run game. Now, when he hurt his hamstring uh against Kansas City, that was him running, and it didn't really occur on a run play. So, then after that, it did become where it was a little bit um harder on him to utilize uh all of his tools, but it really wasn't that part of it. Um, but any exposure is not good for a quarterback or any player. >> Todd, you talked about reps in the preseason and trying to take care of your guys a little bit. Seems like every year like some teams get off slow starts at the start of the season because of that game. Do you sort of anticipate some of that where there's like you're still figuring out who you are, what you do well, and what's the right like what's the timeline on when you expect that? >> I don't know that. I mean, our first two years in Baltimore, I'll just speak offensively, we were a little sluggish and then last year against the Bills, we were not. So, that was not the case. Uh, now we had played them twice the year before, so there was a little bit different um maybe mentality or approach, but I can only compare it to Jacksonville didn't play their starters a heck of a lot more than we played ours. So then it's equal. We're going to go in the same game with basically practicing against other teams. And um I feel like we're going to be fine. I mean, I don't I mean, yesterday's practice, we were out there in the heat, we had the noise cranked up, and our guys were fine. >> When you send everybody for this college weekend, does that also apply to the entire coaching staff? And if so, coming up, I mean, are you able to shut it down at all or what's that going to look like for you guys? Uh Friday we'll start installing. We're practicing against them, but we'll start game planning, really drilling down on Friday. Coaches will have Saturday off and then Sunday morning and we'll be back here uh Sunday afternoon and we'll finish up the game planning uh for the Monday. So really, we'll work tomorrow afternoon after we let the guys go all day Friday and then I mean I'll be in her Saturday morning. I'm a fan like everybody else. I like college football, so I'll be watching college football. And I think I said it up there, maybe I'll bet a horse race or two and try to get my mind off of it and um you know, just to to get a little bit of away, but you can never really get away. Um because then you you you got to prep and be ready. Now, there is a certain point of like we are who we are. Like at this point, it's kind of hard to recreate the wheel of what we've worked on and what we want to continue to kind of drill down on. But yeah, the coaches will have Saturday and Sunday morning off. >> What are the challenges of adding three of your six corners within the last week getting them up to speed? >> Well, I'm excited. I mean, because we didn't have them. >> I mean, the other the other side of it was we didn't have them. We there's a reason why we signed him to come here is because we needed him. We need the depth there. We've had some guys banged up. Um you know, we brought Tim Mat and he got hurt. You know, we had some other guys and so that's just been a tough position in terms of guys getting nicked up. So, I'm excited because obviously we had a deficit there and needed to get some guys in that we think can help us and develop. >> Thank you. All right. Thanks, Dolly.

text: It's really cool. Good to go? All right, we're back. There we go. >> Can't blame you for this one, Tim. Yeah, can't blame you for this one, Tim. >> Uh Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. Uh Joe Milton, looks like he's back. Just your thoughts about how he's feeling and in the process of you had [snorts] to let him go, obviously, for whatever reason, and now you're bringing him back. >> Yeah, I think, you know, one, when he informed me he was coming back, you know, Calvin, I was elated. You know, this is a guy that's worked his butt off to be where he is and develop the way he's developed and the talent is so rare. Um I think, you know, when you're waived or I've been fired many times, you kind of you're in shock a little bit, and then I think you kind of step back and you're like, "Okay, didn't expect this, didn't see this coming." But the more you think about it, you start figuring out the positives and negatives of the situation and you know, for him to be able to stay here with the relationships that he's built, um understanding our system, uh understanding the locker room, the other coaches, um you know, we were thrilled to get him back and um you know, it uh you know, he's going to continue to get better. And that's that's part of it. Got some reps today along with Sam and Dak and all those guys, so um thrilled he's back. >> Well, you you talked about the players who telling you that they appreciate the process in terms of when you had to let somebody go. Did that develop you early as a coach or did that just develop in terms of I want to be as honest as I possibly can so these guys know why you let them go. >> Yeah, I think at the end of the day, I think it's a tough day for everybody. It's a tough day for the person like myself that [clears throat] has to inform them that you're releasing them. It's a tough day for the person that has to hear that news. You know, things, you know, a lot of things go through your mind and I'm big on real relationships and I'm big on having open and honest conversation, but at the end of the day, whether they come back like Joe Milton did or they move on. Um I'm going to leave them and the staff wants to leave them with some feedback of okay, if you're not back when you go to team X spend more time in the special teams coaches office. Spend more time on this or that. Give them some feedback, but we also give them feedback from a positive nature. And so um it's an uncomfortable feeling. You know, they walk in the room, they see you sitting there and they're like, okay, what's going on? And um I just think you want to make it as least less uncomfortable as possible. >> Clarence Hill, Dallas Cowboys. Are you And I know Dak mentioned he was surprised he didn't get picked up. Were you surprised Joe didn't get picked up? Especially considering the things you've said about him and his progress and how he's done in preseason. >> Yeah, totally. But I think you look around the landscape of the league, you know, Clarence, I mean some teams are still holding four, you know, and so um you know, the quarterback rosters and quarterback rooms around the league are pretty crowded right now, but he certainly is talented enough to be claimed, but it's our good fortune that he wasn't. >> Are you glad the chicken controversy is over? I mean, the the 40 controversy is over. >> I think it's a great um a great testament of the way you have to let those things play out, you know, like I don't want to get involved in that, you know, so um two teammates sitting down, talking it out and um they both got new new numbers, so uh there'll be a few more changes. You guys are probably aware of all of them. I don't know all of them, but like I said, one of the first things I learned in this business is when your head coach uh the jerseys are a big deal. I think it starts in college and uh it's a bigger deal now in the NFL than it's certainly ever been. My dad never had to worry about jersey numbers, you know, so um it's uh they'll both look good in their numbers, I know that. >> Mike talked about enjoying being here, you know, and you know, obviously the smile on Dak's face. Have you seen that? I mean, cuz he looks like we we see him like he just really is happy to be with the Cowboys. >> Yeah, I I totally see that. I see it in meetings, I see it on the practice field, I see it him engaging with our his teammates, his brothers. And uh you know, when I look at him, I think he loves What I what I've learned about these players, like last year was Jadaveon. You know, this year Von, these veterans [clears throat] that sit out during training camp, they miss it. I mean, they miss the brotherhood, they miss the time in the locker room, they miss the work, they miss the prep, they miss And so, uh he's been great. >> And not just being missing football, but being a Cowboy. I mean, that that's means so much to him just growing up here. >> Totally. Texas kid, his dad was the biggest Cowboys fan, and uh you know, it'd be awesome to see him put that, you know, helmet on in a real game, you know, up in uh in New York. >> Brian Todd Archer with ESPN. How many other inventive number trades have you been around where guy gave cash, guy gave a dinner, guy whatever. If anything stick out to you? >> Um yeah, I mean, there's been there's been a lot of them. Uh there's been cars, there's been Rolexes. If a guy wants the jersey bad enough and he's been around the league a while, he usually has enough uh capital, cash to get things done. And uh I think these guys found a a way to get this thing resolved. >> Then quarterback play uh with Dak specifically, but the position in general. Spatial awareness, how much is that a big part of a quarterback's DNA? >> Um Todd, I think with the new wave of coverages that we're all seeing, you know, the the days of spot drop three aren't over, but it's a lot smaller where it's, you know, three deep safeties, four underneath, they're dropping to spots. You know, I think the spatial awareness matters now in this new age of cover four, shell, quarters, whatever you want to call it. where you have to get this field space correctly cuz sometimes they're matching certain parts of the field, they're clouding certain parts of the the the other does have hook droppers and things like that. Um and some of the best quarterbacks I've ever been around. One name jumps out to me, that's I'm not going to talk about our guys, but Philip Rivers, his ability to see the field or spatial awareness, another way of saying it is field vision. You know, you feel where everybody is, you know it, you can get through progressions much quicker, and that's usually a good thing when you're having to block these elite pass rushers. So, uh I think it's critical, but I think it's more and more important now because these secondary coaches, the elite ones have gotten to where they're able to change the math and cheat safeties and things like that, so you have to be able to see the full field. >> You have to show with the athletic. With Broderick Jones, um I know it's only been a few days, but is he just getting reps at right tackle? >> Yes. >> And what have you thought of him so >> Uh again, he's doing a great job learning the system, John. He uh you know, very athletic, all the things that we saw. Uh I love how coachable he is. Uh that's one of the things that we heard from one of the people that we talked to, uh is that he would just eat up all the coaching that you could give him, which is usually a great thing. And uh again, he's just, you know, he's he's doing terrific. Um you know, one day he was in shells, that was the first day. Um yesterday he was in pads, learning to play lower. There is some techniques that he's been taught that we're having to retrain. Um you know, the high leg technique is a way you fit double teams and things like that. We don't do that, so he's going to have to learn that. Um and, you know, usually it takes a minute to do that, but in terms of the athlete and the young man, I'm sold uh for him being a Cowboy. >> And entering training camp on paper, you know, that interior offensive line, with the Tylers and Cooper, I mean, it looks great on paper, but watching all of training camp, what have you thought of that group? >> Uh one, they draw a tough match up every day. Um when you talk about going up against, you know, Quinnen and Kenny, Tito, it's a tough match up, but I love the how in sync they are. I think there's just a great chemistry between those those three. >> [snorts] >> And then when you move past those guys, I'd be remiss if I didn't talk about T.J. Bass and the job he's done playing both guard and center. I mean, he's really our number two center right now, probably the first guy in on the inside. Johnny Cornelius is a guy that, you know, when we moved him from tackle to guard, we knew he could play outside, but it things kind of clicked. And so, it's not just those first three guys, but again, I think that you're you're seeing a a gelling of the offensive line, which is important heading into the the the start of the season. >> Dolly. >> Dolly out of the South Carolina Post and Courier. With Joe coming back and being on the practice squad, how does a quarterback like that in that situation develop over the course of the regular season where they're not getting as many reps in practice as they were during the off season? >> Yeah, I mean, you look for opportunities to get him work. He'll I mean, Sam won't take every single rep, you know. Give you guys a great story. I might have said it, but I'm going to say it again. So, when I was QC in Kansas City, uh starter was Elvis Gerbac, Rich Gannon was the backup, and Pat Barnes was the third string quarterback. And Rich was probably I'm guessing, let's say eight years, seven or eight. He's clearly a vested guy. And he would let Pat take all the scout team, but he wanted the third down blitz work because that was the closest you could get to game action. So, Thursday afternoon, third down blitzes, Rich Gannon always like, "Nope, Pat, I got it." And so, there's ways to do that. We're going to get both guys work, make sure Sam gets what he needs to feel prepared, but the development doesn't stop. And you know, I'm going to say this, I think I said to you guys, I don't look at this roster anymore in terms of active and practice squad. We're a family. We're, you know, certainly game day you have to make decisions and stuff, but you know, I don't look at, you know, any of these guys and be like, "Oh, he's a he's a practice squad." They're part of our football team, they're part of our family, and so uh um I think that's important to to impress on them as well. >> More philosophy, but when you're experimenting with new concepts over training camp in the off-season, how much of a leash do you give those in the regular season in terms of trying it if it works for you? If it hasn't in practice, do you try it in a game setting? Do you give it a couple shots, or if it doesn't work, is it not work right away? >> Uh good question. We're a volume offense, we do a lot. Uh we'll always be that way. I think it's important to stress defenses by doing that. And you're going to have your your core plays, your primary plays we call them, and then you have your secondary. Uh I'm open-minded, you know, I'm probably the one that pushes the staff, and they kind of roll their eyes from time to time like, man, that's different, that's new, why are we doing this? But I will say I think when you watch it in practice, if it doesn't look good, it's hard to call it in games, just being honest. Like, you know, that's why I expressed to our guys the importance of practice. Hey, George, if you like this double move, I want it to look good in practice, cuz when I've got my finger and I'm looking at it on, you know, Sunday night in the Meadowlands, I'm going to be like, nah. You know, so I think that's the importance of it, but uh I'm very open-minded about wanting to evolve and, you know, change things, and I'm sure the Giants feel like they know what we're going to we're going to do, and that's that's a good thing, cuz we're always evolving. >> Scott Thompson with the AP. Back on the happy Von Miller briefly, how much is do you think that's helping you guys, and is it maybe helping more even than you anticipated when you all added him? >> Yeah, I think it's just when guys come into this locker room and this organization, I think they're usually pretty happy. We've got a great group of young men that are committed to winning and winning big and winning a world championship, but they're also committed to being there for one another, and whether it's the dinners and stuff that they do, or the groups how they get together, um you know, I think [clears throat] that's that's not unusual. You know, I think it's it's more the norm than not. But uh Von is really happy to be here and uh you feel that in practice, you feel it in meetings and uh what I love about him, he's not you know, he's not afraid to share some ideas and thoughts of things that they did in Denver or some of the other teams he's been and uh I'm always willing to listen. >> You all have been at it for a little more than a month now and next Sunday night the opener out is it so close and yet so far away? Are you eager or anxious to kind of get to that time and >> I don't think so. I'm excited, you know, obviously we're excited. But uh you know, we got to go through the process and uh it's going to be an electric environment. Uh I was the coordinator for the Jets uh in 2011, the 10-year anniversary of 9/11 and uh we played the Cowboys, we won. but uh the uh it's going to be an electric environment, you know, and um I uh uh I have great memories of New York and the fans there and it's going to be uh really cool spectacle for pro football. >> Joe. >> Uh Joe I Dallas Morning News. You've talked about CP's ability to relate to players. How do you see that play out? >> I think it's important when you're communicating in the heat of the moment, the relationships matter. There's a lot of times where you're making a correction and if you don't have the relationship, if you don't have the buy-in from the players at times, players, coaches, they do it as well, can tune you out. I don't think there's any chance of that happening because he's built up the rapport with these guys. Walked by his office this morning, um not surprised. Caleb Downs sitting in there, door closed, watching film. but if you don't have that, I I think it hurts your ability to critique coach, coach hard, call out. I mean, those are all things we do. You know, if guys make a mistake, we we call them out, you know, and that's part of our job and that's part of our job description and they need to know you love them and care about them. And so, if you don't spend the time doing that, then, you know, to me you're you're missing an op. >> Did you anticipate when you guys were interviewing him to it to be to that level? Um and then I guess how unique is his ability on that level? >> Yeah. Nah, no, not really. I wasn't around him until you actually see a guy, working that and doing that and putting the level of importance on it. I don't think you know. So, I think, you know, you'd heard great things. You know, we certainly talked to players that he had coached, >> um you know, both in college and at the pros and they raved about him. They talked about his ability to communicate and to relate. Uh I think it does help the youth. I mean, you know, I didn't go to three nights straight to Jay-Z in New York City. He did. You know, four or five of our players were there, you know? I like Jay-Z, but I wasn't at the concert. So, I do think that the age, you know, uh it does it does help. You know, they're into the same things. He's got some really expensive shoes. He's got some really expensive watches and uh so are players. >> Did you get the Jay-Z invite? >> Uh no. No, I did not. Uh where was I? I was somewhere. Uh but I heard it was a great show and we actually asked what the price of the tickets were and uh I'm not going to uh I'm not going to say what they were, but uh he can afford it. >> The last night was delayed like 4 hours. >> It was. He said he uh didn't come on till like 1:00 in the morning, something like that, yeah. But he said it was an incredible show. But uh yeah, it I I I'm I'm having fun with it, but that's real. I mean, that's real that you can relate to your guys like that. >> Noel Noel Scruggs, NBC 5. Um are you aware of that 35-year-old man who would fake being a 49er player and he milked 26 women out of 1.3 million through romance and investment scheme. And I bring that up because I talked to Mr. Wansley once and he said there were people in town who were impersonating Tony Dorsett and Tony Hill. He said he had to talk with players about that. So, I does this Is that anything that ever crosses your desk? >> Someone mentioned that to me literally the other day, I think walking into a meeting or out of a meeting, I can't remember. And I remember just kind of blowing it off. This is the second time I've heard of it. Um I leave all that stuff to Cable and Wansley and those guys. I mean, you know, what we do is pretty cool. And there's people that would love to be in our shoes and it's incredibly hard to get here. And so, um the fact that people are going to those lengths it doesn't surprise me, but I really don't know anything more about it. >> Were you going to have Boston impersonate you and leave it tabs? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, yeah, they can't. How you going to How you going to replace this? I mean, you know. >> Garrett. >> Garrett from CBS Sports. You talked about when you first got here the importance of like locker room location for players. Quinnen's right in the middle now next to Dak. Kind of What does that say about how much >> And by GP. >> What? >> Couple of Alabama boys. Do you guys know that they played on the same pee wee team? I bet they didn't lose many games. >> So, what does that kind of show and kind of what you expect and anticipate from Quinnen this year? >> Uh well, good leading. So, I will announce the four captains that were just selected this morning for the 2026 NFL season. On defense, you have Quinnen Williams. On defense, you have Kenny Clark. On offense, you have Dak Prescott. And on special teams, you have Brandon Aubrey. Uh but back to your question about Quinnen is from the minute he got here he's been about one thing and it's winning. You know, he's never He's never won in the NFL. And the leadership is real, the talent's incredible. Uh but every decision that that guy makes is based on what's best for us winning. And I love that about him, and it's infectious. It rubs off. And uh I love hearing him talk to the young linemen and and the young defenders. And you know, he was very very very involved in, you know, some of the things that we did from helping the defense, you know, grow and learn and and all that stuff. So, uh terrific young man, great dad. Um he and Miranda you know, great parents. And just thrilled to have him here, man. >> Is your process with the captains, is that all player voting or is that >> All player voting. Yep. Uh do you pop in with CP next week during his game planning at any point? Uh just to see how things are going in his >> Yeah, all the time. You know, uh if I can't get in there, he has a list of, you know, things from practice to notes. But um yeah, I learned a lot last year, Nick, in terms of how to manage my time and be involved in all three phases. And there's no question in my mind I'll be better this year uh at that than I was last year. Um and I'm not in there to second-guess. I'm in there to I shoot I showed him a blitz look today of something that we have that we could make a little bit better with a tweak or make it not better, harder uh on the offense by doing something. And uh it was great conversation. He does that. And then I brought him in to talk about a a route concept and that we've been struggling with. And I said, "Hey, what about this and this?" Last year, there was more guys closer together. And um again, I just I'm the one that separates them based off of the numbers. >> The other thing is, so you your defense will not have a chance to play together until next week. Practice is practice, a game's a game. What do you think is the key, while they're learning each other, what's the key to keeping their head above water and surviving, getting results until they can develop that innate wordless communication? >> Yeah, I think at the end of the day, you we probably won't reinvent the wheel. You know, we're going to do what we do well, which going against them every day in practice, there's a lot of things that we do really, really well. Um you know, the communication has been something that's been non-negotiable from the time that we started with with CP and in his staff. And one of the things that we did was we'd give him, you know, I think we gave him like 5 minutes to come up with your first defensive meeting about, you know, identity and play style and stuff like that. And uh I don't remember exactly what he said. I could pull the the video, but uh he was awesome. >> Was it the same message that he gave when he actually did it? >> It was, yeah. It was. Uh it wasn't uh too different. >> Is that it? Good. Thanks, guys. Enjoy your weekend. >> You too.

title: Colts' Keenan Allen responds to arrest, Steichen names Richardson QB2
text: Um, in regards to Keenan Allen, um, obviously there's a legal situation going on right now and I'm going to keep everything in-house uh, in that regard. Um, as far as the backup quarterback, um, Anthony will will be our backup quarterback. Um, I thought he did some good things um, through camp. He's continued to develop and grow and learn and continue to get better. Uh, and same thing with Riley. Um, he's continued to learn, grow, and get better and with both those guys just consistency and that's going to be um, you know, part of their job going through this this season, getting those scout team reps. Um, that's going to be big for them um, because you never know, you know, when their number could get called. Um, as far as captains, we voted on captains, announced captains. Um, DeForest Buckner will be a captain, Kemoko Turay. Um, Quenton Nelson, uh, Jonathan Taylor, and Daniel Jones and uh, really excited for those guys. Obviously a captain I think is one of the biggest honors in the National Football League. Um, so to be named a captain by your teammates, they trust you um, to uphold the standard every day. So, excited for those guys. >> Who was ultimately the separator between Anthony and Riley? >> Um, I thought Anthony, you know, played some better ball in the preseason. Um, you know, I think uh, both of them had pretty good camps. All the you know, things they can both improve on. Um, but I thought he did some good things in the games. >> Will Riley be emergency third on game day? >> Yeah, most likely, yeah. >> When it comes to Keenan, I know you said keep things in-house, but what was your you know, reaction and how emotional did it get for you? >> Yeah, I know, I got a lot of respect for Keenan. Um, and you know, I had private conversations with him. Um, like I said, we'll keep that in-house and keep that private. >> With Anthony, um, obviously it's been quite the journey for him throughout his career. What have you I guess learned and respect about just what he's put in? >> Yeah, I think uh, he's grown a ton um, just as an individual, you know, a young player in this league, learning, going through adversity, um, going through, you know, things, uncontrollable things, injuries that he's had to battle through. Um, like we've said all along, he's a very talented player um, and he stuck with it and kept grinding. Um, you know, and he's in the same spot, you know, he was last year um, after the competition. And so, I'm excited for him and his growth going forward. >> After getting through training camp and preseason, what's the excitement level just to get the season going? >> Very excited. Um obviously it's here. Um we had our last practice today. Obviously we got the 3-day break. Um but it's here and we're excited to you know Baltimore's going to be a hell of a test at home and we're excited for that challenge. I know our guys are excited um to play at home week one from our home crowd. So um our guys will be ready to go. Just you know pure excitement there. >> So is there like any update on Alie? He's looking >> Yeah, he looked good. Um he practiced full today. Um he looked pretty good. Um he did some good things for us. Um and um I'm excited where he's at. >> So full he's in team and everything? >> He was running team drills and all that stuff today, yep. >> In training camp and preseason, would you say this is one of the healthier teams you've had going into this >> Yeah, very Yeah, very very it is. Um obviously we had our nicks and bruises early but you know to be healthy week one is huge for our football team and you know credit to Mike Minnis and our training staff. We try to do a great job um you know preparing and planning for training camp and how that all goes to make sure our guys are healthy and ready to go while also keeping the conditioning up and making sure guys are in tip-top shape to start the season. >> Yeah, we talked about Anthony and the pros of using him potentially in a short yardage package. I think most people know the pros. What are the cons of why you wouldn't want to do that anyway? >> I mean I haven't really thought about that, the cons. Um obviously you know we'll take everything into consideration and then we'll go from there. >> Opened the season with a home win last year. How important is it to to get a win in the home opener to to start the season? >> Yeah, it's very important. I think every season you want to start fast and you want to finish strong but starting your season fast, we know it's a long season but to get that first one especially in AFC opponent um who's a good football team, it'll be a very important for us. >> Why do you feel the need to let me ask you why did you want to announce the backup now? I know you said you could have waited until >> Cuz I think just from a mindset standpoint, you know knowing that you are the backup quarterback going into week one um that you're prepared and ready um to go if something happens. >> Shane, will Keenan's playing time be altered at all? >> Um no, he'll play week one. Yep. >> Anyone else? >> you have >> good sense of of how you'll use him yet? Not routes and that sort of thing, but just how much and role and that sort >> Yeah. Yeah, we got a good feel for that. We'll keep that all in house, but yeah, we got a real good feel for that. >> Okay. >> I don't think we asked you about it when it happened last week, but Rigoberto getting the contract extension. >> Yeah. >> What has he just provided for you in terms of reliability? >> Consistency. I mean, I went over in the team meeting today talking about his consistency and how consistent he's been here for so many years. Um, just the ball placement um, the built-up reps from him and Luke, those two guys together um, has been phenomenal. Um, and then like I said, just the consistency that he brings to this football team when we need to punt the ball, um, he's darn accurate, you know, down the field and placing those balls, especially, you know, when we got to get them backed up. Um, he's been phenomenal his whole career doing that. >> Anthony, what was your reaction to being named the QB2? >> Um I was on it. You know, um, I'm just blessed. I'm just blessed to continue to, you know, uh, find a way in this league, continue to, uh, find my way on a on a roster. I'm just thankful that they believe in me enough to, you know, promote me uh, QB2. And I'm just, you know, ready to work and I'm just willing to work for this team and just, you know, provide, you know, my best self, you know, for this squad to just help us win. >> This is kind of This is where you were last year at this time back at Does it feel different or how you got here or not? >> Um, not necessarily. Honestly, um, this year and last year, you know, I've been trying to put in the work. I still I feel like I still got a lot of more work to put in. Um but, you know, like you just said, I was in the same position last year. You know, uh, God put me in a position to, you know, make sure I'm ready. I got to stay ready, uh, so my number and my name is called, I could just go out there and do my thing. >> How gratifying is it though, Anthony, because you've been through a lot, especially the last year with the injuries like that, to have the opportunity to be trusted in a position like this? >> Man, uh, I'm extremely grateful, you know, um, adversity, you know, I love adversity. I love life. I I read the Bible a lot, so the more I can see you to, you know, step into my faith. I I read a lot of stories about people who deal with adversity and, uh, try to keep their faith, you know, over fear and uh adversity brings a lot of fear cuz there's a lot of uncomfortable situations that's that's thrown into your life, but you know, I'm trying to continue to have my faith over my fear and just you know, keep pursuing and then just keep being a better person, better man, and better player and you know, I'm just grateful I get to have another shot to do it. >> Earlier this week Chris told us you will be in Indianapolis for this year. Going from the the trade request to now, what's kind of changed for you? >> Um not much has really changed. Honestly, when I reported back for OTAs, you know, I was here. Told myself I was going to be here and prepare myself like I was going to be here for the start of the season and you know, God made it happen. So, you know, I'm still trying to do the same thing, prepare myself and just get ready for day one. >> Where do you think you've improved the most this offseason? >> Um I feel like I've done a little bit better when it comes to managing the game, you know, not trying to make the big plays all all the time, you know, just manage the game, do the the boring things when they're just right there in front of me, but um feel like I can still improve and just command the offense a little bit more and just following Daniel's footsteps a little bit. >> Anthony, do you notice the eye issue at all anymore? >> Uh when exactly? >> The eye issue when you're out there playing, do you notice it impacting you at all? >> No, not really. Honestly, just every day as I continue to just wake up and go through my daily life, my vision and stuff continues to adjust and just improve and you know, I feel like I've been pretty good out there on the field. >> Anthony, is the trade request on the table at all or have you taken it back? >> No, man. I'm here. You know, I'm not really thinking about that. I haven't talked to my agent about that in a minute, honestly, since the day one of camp, you know, I've just been preparing, trying to prepare myself to be, you know, the backup for Daniel and I got granted that today. So, that's my main focus, you know, I'm trying to make sure I can just elevate myself. So, God's willing my name and number is called, I can go out there and perform. >> Thanks, Anthony. >> Just what what do you kind of what's the past few days been like I suppose and just what have you kind of told your teammates about and what did or didn't happen and so forth? >> Uh going keep the discussions in in house. I just focus on being a good football player and ready for the season. >> What was your reaction to the arrest and perhaps how do you move forward from there? >> Because it's ongoing legal matter, we're not going to discuss it. Like I said, just focus on football and being a good team. >> Has has it gotten in the way of anything this week football wise? >> I'm not discussing it. How how was the week of practice for you? Just another week of getting further integrated and do you feel like you're where you need to be right now? >> It was a great week. Pretty hot outside. Feel like we got some good conditioning in we needed it. Yeah, it was good for us. >> How are you feeling? >> I'm feeling good. Ready to go. >> There's a new number for you again out there 11. Is that what you're rocking with this year? >> Yeah, I think so. I don't know. Tried tried it out today. I thought it was pretty sweet. 10 looked good too, so you know, we'll keep it keep it going and open up pitchers wins Monday, so probably figure out figure something out by then. >> You haven't decided yet then. So it's up in the air. >> It's up in the air. We'll see Monday. >> Kaepernick, what do you want fans to know about you that you know, that this is their first impression of you it's not a fortunate one. What do you want them to know about you? >> I take my job serious. I'm a good football player. You know, and I try to be a good good teammate and yeah, that's what I'm focused on. >> Just a mistake? I'm asking the question. >> No, we're not discussing anything. >> Do you think you expect to be punished in any way for what happened? >> It's an ongoing legal matter, so whatever. >> With the number did we have to wear 13? >> A little bit. Seeing Tread in it and then hearing people call him 13. It's a little it's a little weird. Now every time I hear 13 I keep looking at him. >> I know there's not a lot you can discuss, but is there anything you'd like to say to fans or anything along the lines of what happened? >> Yeah, just appreciate the support. I'm going to play football this year. I'm going to play this year. Just angle. >> I think I have the support of I think Chris Balas went to bat for your character and things like that. >> Yeah, it's big, uh, like I said, we're going to keep that in house, supporting everything. >> Even body-wise, how's it felt getting out here now, week plus? Uh, I know last year you guys Chicago made a little bit earlier. How's it felt being out here? >> It's been great. Uh, like I said, a little hot a little hot this week for whatever reason, but, um, you know, it it was good work for us. Got to I was able to run around and, um, you know, get with the guys, go against the ones, get some good work in, so good good for going in, uh, week one. >> Can you recap your preseason and just what it meant to come through at at a critical time like that for your future? >> Yeah, it was, uh, it was a crazy preseason. I think it was one of the most mentally challenging battles that I've been through. It was really good for me. I, man, like when I think about the situation, I I feel bad for Blake, too, cuz I feel like both of us kind of earned that, and it was all that I could do to keep up with him during fall camp and just try to stay even. He was kicking at such a high level, and it just continually reminded me just to compete against myself every single day. Um, and then finally kind of felt like myself towards the end and just prepared and did well in the games, and then literally it came down to the wire. I had no idea what was going to happen when they made the final decision, and I really tried to emotionally prepare myself for whatever the outcome was going to be. And so, you know, Mace calls me and tells me I'm going to be a starting for the Colts, and I was like, "Okay." Like, and he's kind of like, "That's it? Like, that's your reaction?" I'm like, "Well, no, I'm incredibly grateful and blessed, and, you know, I was praying about that and working towards that, but you just have to prepare yourself emotionally for any outcome." And, um, kind of took a while for that to set in, for it to feel real and be like, "Okay, like, let's go. Let's get ready for week one." Because to us, you know, it's like every I think people from the outside are like they look at it preseason and it's like whatever, do the games really matter? Do they count? But to us, like, that's our life, you know, every single day, and you're battling and battling and battling, and so much goes into it. Um, and so I do feel extremely blessed and grateful to be here. I can't wait, and now it's just preparing for that week one mentality and building off what I was able to do in preseason. >> How were you able to stay locked in with so much pressure going on? >> You know, I I have a really good support system around me. Uh it's always hard during camp because it's 12-13 hours a day of football. And so, you you only have so much mental capacity. So, when you're filling your mind with just football and performance and uh comparison for so long, it does wear on you. And so, I really had to focus on stoicism, reading books, praying, and trying to bring myself out of that mindset. You know, you go out there and perform badly in a practice and you're like, "Oh my gosh, like what's going to happen now?" So, it was really, really difficult. Camp is always a physical battle, not as much for us specialists as it is a mental battle. And every single day trying to pull myself out of a of a bad mentality if things went well, and if things went really good, trying to bring myself down to neutral every day. >> So, I'm sorry. Physically, how do you feel? Do you feel 100%? And is there a difference between being like cleared and being yourself again? >> Yeah, there's definitely a difference between being cleared and being yourself again. Um I felt that in OTAs when I was cleared, but I was working to be what I felt like last year. And I think when you come off of an injury, um probably any of these guys will tell you that have dealt with these injuries, you can't really compare yourself to what you were. Um you have to get stuck in this mentality of how do I become a better version of me every single day.
