title: LIVE: Kellen Moore Media Availability 9/3/2026
text: [music] >> Mhm. >> [music] >> Look at this spot. Good setup. [laughter] >> We can just watch practice from >> Yeah, it's a good spot. Um Yeah, I don't really have a whole lot. Zach Wilson won't be at practice. Uh he went back just cuz he had a baby right before training camp. So, he's just going back uh with the family for the day. So, other than that, everyone will be here. >> I thought you said he went back to school. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, who knows? >> But Kevin, you drafted these guys. You like them, obviously. But where do you see Bryce's biggest jump in development? >> Yeah, I'd just say the uh physicality. I think for a bigger kid, obviously, that's going to be an important part, particularly in the run game. Thought he's been a really physical player. We know he's fast, but the physicality. And then just the mental stuff's always the challenge for these guys. I thought he's done a good job picking it up. >> Did Bryce and Dorian progress faster than rookies typically do fourth and sixth round from your experience like throughout camp or >> I would say the way training camp went, they ended up having a lot more opportunities probably than we thought, and then they took advantage of those. yeah, a couple injuries, a couple uh you know, uh Jaylen stepping away from football, uh a couple things happened like that, and all of a sudden they're playing a lot. And so, they did a great job. >> Kevin, how do you think maybe you could get a sense of just how the expectations are >> Um I mean, I'd say our team has confidence. yeah, I think we finished well last year. Feels like a long time ago now, but um yeah, I think our guys are excited about this. They're excited about the opportunity to go compete. We're going to open up with one of the top teams in the league in Detroit. It's going to be a lot of fun. Uh we know what an NFL season's going to take. There's going to be some highs, there's going to be some lows. And so, uh I think we got the right kind of guys to navigate it. >> How have you seen Martin Emerson evolve like these past couple of weeks? And um what's impressed you the most about him as of late? >> I think it was a little bit of an adjustment just coming off of an injury in particular, but also it it's a very different scheme from what he played uh in Cleveland. And both both schemes are really really successful. And so, uh it was just some new techniques, some new adjustments for him. I think you saw that as he went through the whole training camp. You can see what the back half of training camp looked like. It looked really good. And so, I think credit to him as far as adapting and adjusting and and then just getting back to, you know, the version of him that he always wants to be coming off that injury. It takes a little bit of time to come off of those. >> How big of a role do you see him kind of having for this defense with this team? And yeah, how much do you think you guys will rely on him? >> Yeah, he's done a nice job. And I think for him, you know, he's he's going to have opportunities throughout the season. I think that's just inevitably what the NFL is about. And so, you know, he's just he'll be ready to maximize it. He's played a lot of football, I think. So, the credit to him will be that he'll be ready to go. >> How close are Prince and Caesar to coming back to practice? Are they fully participating >> Yeah, pretty much. I think maybe not quite 100%, but you know, they've done they've done a great job. >> And what do you make of the way that Chase has played over the last 6, 7 years now? He's in the prime of his career, but he's in the prime of his career, but he's still improving with his pass rush. >> I'd just say Chase's work ethic is really special. You know, what he does all off-season, getting himself prepared. And when you watch a training camp practice, even an in-season practice, his effort shows up. You know, you can see that he's trying to get better each and every day. And so, you know, our exposure the last year and a half, he's just done a really really good job. >> What's going to be your message to the guys two days off here and you have to work to get >> Yeah, obviously recharge, you know, recharge the battery, so to speak, get our get our energy back coming off of a really good training camp. You know, for our guys, it's about, you know, enjoying it, spending a little bit of time with family or friends. And you know, I'm sure a few of our guys will go to college games. That's kind of the the fun fun thing to do. You know, they've just got to make sure they're moving their bodies a little bit, get a little bit activity in their bodies. So, when they come back Monday, we'll kind of have a bonus day and then we'll get into a normal week. >> Did that when you were in the NFL like the challenge to that for you do you have to put in like extra work so to say that >> I would say a lefty QB, my experience. Especially in the backup roles. The offense is all built around a righty QB. So like when I was in Detroit, Matthew was our starter. Sean Hill or Dan Orlovsky was the backup and I was usually the third stringer. So no plays are designed for lefties, so you're just going to have to figure it out. I remember Joe Lombardi trying to call a few plays and I just said, "Hey, just call it for a righty and I'll flip it in my own mind. It'll be fine." I think for some people, I think there's been some instances where maybe having a lefty backup, some people don't necessarily like it if there's a righty QB that's a starter. And so I think that definitely is real. With the game playing more shotgun, I think there's a little bit less dependence on that, but I was fortunate I was with you know Scott Linehan. Nuss is a lefty. He had Nuss way back in Idaho. He had a few other guys in his coaching career that were lefties, so I think he's had three or four, so it was no big deal for Scott. >> [clears throat] >> I mean there there's been a few. I mean it it's >> Not many though, surprisingly. >> Yeah, there there's not too many, but there's been a few and I think uh you know, obviously just the direction of a lot of times it's the play action game that you have to kind of direct. And sometimes that ties into the run game based off your your scheme. And so there can be a few challenges there, but uh yeah, I think sometimes it's more of a flavor thing for certain coaches that like it or dislike it. We'll see. >> We'll see. Obviously, you know, I'm proud of Hunter the way he navigated this past year and so uh yeah, we'll see we'll see how all this stuff goes. >> When you say call it for a righty and I'll flip it, what are you talking about? The selection of >> The direction sometimes with the play action and the formation, so uh I know for example when I was with Joe, who you know, Joe's the best. Uh he was with Drew for all those years, so everything was based off the righty QB, all the play actions for those like boot keepers to the right, you know, that Drew would always launch these post routes for touchdowns. And then, you know, then he had to call it for a lefty and for Joe it was just like, I've never called it this way. So, just call it for as like you're a righty and I'll just I'll flip it. It's my job. It's my fault anyways I'm a lefty. So, >> uh couple of play actions were kind of the same way with that, so >> Did you ever have to go right and like throw with the left or like you ever throw with the worst arm? >> No, no, no. No, I I'm still good to go and uh yeah. I remember when I was at Boise they never ran, you know, a play action called naked uh where you keep the ball away from the outside zone and it was always naked right. It never they never even called naked left before. And so, while I was battling for the QB position, it was still naked right no matter what they said, "Until you win the job, we're never going naked left." And then once I won it then they had to go the other [laughter] way, so >> Was there ever a point when you were when you were younger that you like tried to become a righty? >> No, no. I enjoyed the lefty thing. I I I took pride in it. There's only so many of us. >> Did you have a lefty that you watched growing up that you really liked? >> Um I mean you had the Steve Young, Matt Leinart uh was kind of you know, peak college um it was probably right around when I was in high school, so uh probably a couple of those. >> You never had to worry about being a catcher. >> No. To be honest, I chose probably the wrong sport, so >> lefties are supposed to go to baseball. >> One other little detail I'm curious about progression. [clears throat] Like Did Did you have to Did you have to kind of reverse that or did you have Like how did you even manage? >> Literally the plays would just be flipped completely. So, yeah. Which usually any lefty QB who grew up as a lefty QB, you know, most of the drills are all righty driven. You just have to be a mirror. And you learn to figure it out. Okay. Awesome. What's up? Thanks.

title: Mike Vrabel on Heading Into Week 1: "We Try to Be As Consistent As We Possibly Can."
text: Hello. >> Hey. >> Hey, how are you? >> I am great, Mike. >> Does it help in any >> [clears throat] >> way, or has it helped in your prep, uh the fact that you did play Seattle 7 months ago? >> I mean, I don't think that it I mean, as far as the the players that they've had and the and the play style, um maybe. I mean, we'll we'll have to block them better. Uh we'll have to to be able to run football better. We'll have to be able to um stop the run better. I mean, there's a lot of things that we're going to have to do better uh based on the personnel that they have. Um you know, they may do some of the same things. They may change. We'll have to be ready for for a lot of those, but um I mean, I think that the the the the players are there, the ones that contributed heavily and that are there, you know, really good players that we're going to have to to understand their play style and what they do and how they rush and and how they you know, block. And I think that's been about the only thing that you can really take away from it and just be ready for you know, the style that we think that that they may run offensively and defensively. >> Obviously, different players respond in different ways to different situations, but in your experience, is there any way to adequately prepare a rookie for his first NFL experience, especially when you go into a game with the experience? >> to give them as much as we can here and and and stress them as much as we possibly can in in practice and in noise and situations and but probably not. You know, I mean, I don't know if there's a great way to be able to do that um for their first game and the experiences and the the emotions that they're going to have. Um And but it also be something that they'll never forget. >> And Mike, related to the Super Bowl, Sean McVay coming off his first Super Bowl talked about that it it was killing him that he got outcoached in the game. In your reflecting on the Super Bowl, did you think that you and your staff were out coached in that game? >> I mean, I'm not going to reflect back on it. We say the same thing every time we lose. We get out coached, we get out played. Um, when we win, it's it's on our players, but you know, that's a long time ago. We'll need to to play better, we'll need to coach better to give ourselves a chance in that environment. And um you know, it's always been the same. You know, we try to be as consistent as we possibly can. You know, after wins and then after losses, you're always looking for things that you could have done differently as a coach and and as a player. >> As you build this team, how much of what you did in the off season was based upon what you learned about the group in in the Super Bowl and areas that you wanted to to improve? >> Um you know, I I don't think that the Super Bowl um was the only factor in in the decisions that we made. I think you you evaluate your roster. You know, you look at the guys that you want to move forward with and the guys that you feel like, you know, that maybe moved on in free agency. Um you know, you look at the draft and you try to figure out who the best guys that that would come onto your team that you have a vision for. So I mean, the the games that we all every game that we played, I think factors into it. You know, you just you have to be at your best uh in in this league in every moment, you know, whether that's going on the road in Seattle, it's playing at home, or playoff games. >> Mike, as a player, what's the biggest difference you see in Drake from the guy who walked off the field in the Super Bowl to the guy who's going to be going into Seattle next week? >> Well, I think just more comfort in what we're doing, more more command, more understanding to be able to you know, operate and get us into the best plays. I think there's probably a comfort level with Um once you know your job really, really well, you can help other people do their job, and and hopefully that that's the case where you know, he's sharing details of the play with with guys that are in there, or he's getting guys lined up, or making sure that you know, we're legal, or the timing of the motions, and I think as the as you understand the your knowledge increases, uh hopefully the details do as well. >> Mike, this probably this probably relates to what Andrew was just asking in terms of Christian Gonzalez. Is he a better player today than he was the when we saw him in in February? And if so, how? >> Yeah, I mean, again, I I he's put a lot of great work in and the competitiveness in practices. You know, he's never really stressed. There's a very He's a very I think comfortable, and I don't mean that by lazy. It's just that he's not stressed, and then when he bursts, he bursts, and you know, when he has a chance to go for an interception, he does. When he has a chance to, you know, stab, he makes great decisions. Um you know, he plays square, and he's athletic and fast. So, I I mean, I've seen a a I mean, it's not a player that's been sitting around here just waiting. You know, I mean, it's a player that's every chance that he has looked to improve, challenge, two-minute situations, normal down and distances, third down. I've seen a very competitive player. >> Mike, there was something reported earlier this week on the contract stuff. I was wondering what what your reaction to that was, and what the organization's reaction was. Christian's trainer went on the radio, talked about some of the contract negotiations. >> Yes, sir, I didn't hear you. >> Yeah, I was talking over you. Um no, again, no no no comments or nothing new to report with Christian, other than I mean, I think I pretty much covered everything I could there with Mike's question, but uh nothing new to report contractually. Um Trying to get him ready for the football game. Trying to get him ready on the first and second down stuff that we're doing today. And and how that how he can help us win. >> Last time we talked to Christian, Mike, he did not commit to playing week one without a new contract. Would you and your coaching staff have to create a plan without him for this game against Seattle? you know, we we have to prepare for everything that potentially happen or whether that's uh player's availability through multiple different reasons. So, we'll have to be ready for for a lot of things and as we work here into week one and and the craziness of the National Football League and the journey that we're about to go on. >> Mike, is is there much concern that the longer this thing draws out, that it's just continuing to be a distraction for Christian and something that's negatively affecting maybe his relationship with the team? >> Um I think we want to try to be uh as ready and prepared for the football game as we possibly can. You know, I think distractions come um in a lot of different ways and it's how we handle them, how we respond to them. So, again, I I love coaching Christian. I I he's a valuable member of this football team and you know, we'll continue to have discussions and and but I don't have anything else to add about the contract. >> Mike, are you expecting Christian to play in Seattle? >> Uh as I repeated as I said a couple days ago, as the head coach, I expect every player that's healthy and under contract to to practice and to play. And again, that may change based on my conversations with different players and the plan that they have each and every day when you talk about practice or what the plan may be for the for the football game. So, that goes with this situation and anybody else that would would fall underneath that that that's what our expectation is. >> Mike freak head has talked about one thing he wanted to work on this year is getting the ball out quickly among many things that he's working on and I just wanted to ask you what you've observed from him through the practices and if you can really assess that when you're not >> I think that that's great but there's also a design that they play and there's a timing element to when we can get the ball out quickly based on the the route based on the depth of the route on the location of the route and we can't just raise it up and throw it the second that we get it every single snap but you know we went through a lot of details this morning about you know our first and second down offense and and listen to the players answer offensively about some of the details and the different plays that and the concepts that we have on first and second down and I think it was very reassuring just to hear the different positions and the different players talk about each of those details. So there's times when the ball can come out quick and there's certainly times when when it can't based on the the concept that we have. >> Speaking of the three captains I'm curious [clears throat] your thoughts on Drake London Morgan Robert Kevin and Marcus Dean you know named captains this season. >> I mean those guys have you know since I've been here um you know the the the five that that were here last year were were great leaders and very consistent players very consistent demeanor uh in their preparation and the type the type of teammates that they were we added Kevin uh this year so uh I'm always appreciative of those guys that that lead will have a leadership group as well that will assist them and again we'll meet but it's not like we have to have a standard meeting for them to to approach me and and talk about something. >> Like the athletic um released or published its findings uh after its review into Diana Rossini's reporting. Curious if you have any reaction to that. >> no, I don't have any reaction. No, we've moved on and focused on Seattle and focused on the Patriots and focused on getting better this week. >> Do you feel like that situation is fully behind you? >> Uh, try to just say that I've moved on and I'm excited about this new opportunity here as we start this season. >> Your final question. >> You were talking about dialing You were talking about dialing back before ramping up over the course of the the game week there. Is this the day when it's kind of full speed ahead or is that Wednesday? >> Uh, no, we'll we'll go at with some speed today. Uh, I mean, we only get 14 padded practices through 17 weeks. 11 of which have to be, uh, in the first 11 weeks. So, and we'll be in the shells. We'll have to start to learn how to practice with shells on without shoulder pads. Uh, which I think is something that good teams know how to do. I think that they, um, can can go with speed and it's not a jog through. There's speed, but there's no collisions. Um, but there's has to be contact. It's it's practice. We have to get these reps for first and second down. So, um, no, I'm looking forward to seeing, you know, where we're at here going into the first and second down offense. >> Thanks, guys. Appreciate it.

title: Football at Four: Explaining Some Surprising Recent Eagles Roster Decisions
text: Josh play for Mike Gill here on the sports bash all [music] nice 3 ESPN. Yes, it is time for football at 4. Andrew the Czecho is back. [music] And don't forget as it is each and every day football at 4 being brought to you by Ocean Casino Resort, the best place for game days. The Fanatic Sports Book at Ocean Casino's gallery bar booking games. Ocean's go-to game day destination with huge screens, great drinks, and all the sports book action you want. It's a perfect place to catch every play and celebrate every win. Learn more at the oceanac.com. And Andrew is someone who doesn't just cover the Eagles for insidethebirds.com along with the inside the birds pod, but he is someone who has been closely watching this team as we got to the initial 53man roster. We want to get Andrew's perspective as we've been talking throughout the week, you know, what do we know about the roster now and what it could mean moving for forward. First of all, Andrew, welcome back into the show. How you doing today, >> Josh? I'm doing well. Thanks for having me on. >> I appreciate you jumping on today because, you know, one of the conversations we were having with Jeff Mosher yesterday, I thought was very interesting, which is kind of maybe some of the why behind some of these decisions with the roster. And for me, Andrew, I want to go to tight end first because we've had so many conversations about what this offense could be and what we know about the history of guys like Shawn Manion and others. And we know Dallas led this team in touchdowns last year, but he also has a history of injuries. So, as you look at the tight end position, they drafted Eli Sters, right? They kept Jenkins on the roster. Grant Calcara is on injury reserve. Johnny Munt, he's basically here for blocking from what I've been able to surmise. So, what is your perspective on the state of the tight end room for the Eagles as of right now? >> Yeah, that one's probably the most confounding to me, Josh. When you talk about Dallas, you also have to talk about the injury history. Yes, last year he missed just one game. That was the Kansas City Chiefs game in week two. But apart from that, health has been a bit of a challenge. And so you look about what that could mean and he's another year older now. So your tight end room would then be as you outlined Johnny Muntz, you have EJ Jenkins and Eli Sters. This whole matter is complicated by the fact that Eli Sters has been a little bit slow in terms of his progression. So it's not quite clear when he will be able to contribute to the Eagles and I can't imagine it would be early in the season. So I know that in a West Coast offense you're going to prioritize the tight end. So, it wasn't really a surprise to me that they rostered four. It was the four that they chose to keep. Now, I've noted this in my observations that EJ Jenkins had impressed me at different stages of training camp in terms of his blocking prowess. He has a a receiving background. He was a collegiate wide receiver. Played for three universities. Got to the Eagles at about 240 245 lbs at 6'6. blossom into 260 pounds and really took to the blocking aspect. I remember talking to him for a couple years now about that. He takes a lot of pride in that. Spent a lot of time working with tight ends coach Jason Michael. He's no longer there. And Dallas Goddard and picking their brains. And I think he was just more of a well-rounded player relative to Cameron Lu who I didn't think had a particularly strong camp. brings so much to the special teams group that it was a little bit of a surprise that they leaned uh Jenkins in that. But there's a big question there and I think because of you have two blocking centric tight ends, you have a rookie who isn't where the Eagles need him to be at this point. He's not ready for prime time and then you have Dallas Goddard, that would be a position that I could I would imagine the Eagles may look to to fortify uh at some point. You know, and it's interesting because you mentioned Fortify, you know, how he does have a history of making trades, you know, right before the season, in season trades. Do you think it's a trade that might be the kind of way or do you think this might be a situation where the Eagles keep giving a close eye maybe on guys who could maybe hit the waiver wire? It might be a situation where the Eagles could take advantage of somebody else's roster shuffling. >> Well, Hi Roseman's always going to leave no stone unturned. And I think at least if it were me, I would let this play out a little bit in the early part of the season, see what you have, evaluate from there. It may not be as dire as what it looks like on paper. So, you kind of have to let things develop, but I I would imagine that you're going to need a little bit more of a reinforcement than someone on a practice squad or a waiver wire. It would have to be via trade. Maybe it's a free agent who's out there. But I I think right now what I would do is kind of just let things play out and see what you have and then kind of go from there. >> Andrew, the other position that I I feel like the entire world is trying to get more clarity on is what do you think the reasoning is for keeping all four quarterbacks because it wasn't like Cole Payton was a guy that there there was a ton of teams around the league that were I mean I I heard stories that there people were trying to convert him to a tight end or other position. So, why do you think the Eagles felt the need to keep all four quarterbacks on the initial 53? >> Well, the Eagles prioritized the quarterback position, Josh, perhaps more than any other team. Now, it was not a very fruitful summer for Andy Dalton and Tanner McKe. I thought for much of training camp, Andy Dalton had the slight edge. Tanner McKe closed out a little bit, a little stronger, but then you have the preseason game where he fell flat. that Andy Dalton finished a little stronger um in terms of preseason play. So, no one really emerged. But then you have a young quarterback in Cole Payton and it was widely expected that he's going to be a developmental prospect. It's going to take some time, especially mechanically, but when you have a quarterback with those kind of traits and that athleticism who can maybe offer a multifaceted skill set, you saw him rep a little bit on special teams in the preseason finale. That's not a player that you want to risk parting with. And I think a lot of that, if you're Hi Roseman, I would imagine you look at Kyle McCord, who they drafted last year in the sixth round out of Syracuse, didn't get nearly the amount of reps that Cole Payton got in training camp, goes elsewhere to the Green Bay Packers, lights it up in training camp, gets traded to the Miami Dolphins, and now he's their backup quarterback. You don't want to risk losing another young player. You want to continue to to work with them and develop them. They call themselves the quarterback factory for a reason. And I I think some every every season, every every roster transaction can be viewed as a learning experience. And I think maybe that Kyle McCord uh situation there factored into it. And the Eagles really value that position. So they they view it as we have a veteran in Andy Dalton who's 38 years old. He started a number of games in this league. He's entering his 16th season. He's been in multiple offenses. he can be a very effective sounding board and another set of eyes on the field for Jaylen Herz. You have Tanner McKe who the organization still values. I can tell you that internally there is still a lot of optimism regarding Tanner McKe. It didn't work out for him this summer. Perhaps he was a little bit slow to to grasp this offense and he looked a little hesitant there, but I I don't think that their view of him has dampered any. So, they all bring something different to the table is what I'm getting at. >> Absolutely. That's kind of what Nick Fos was saying on his season podcast about how you know Andy Dalton, he probably knows more than some of the coaches do about certain systems and defenses and he could be a great guy for all the quarterbacks in that room. Andrew Deco joining us football and forward powered by the inside the birds podcast inside the birds.com looking at the Eagles roster the initial 53 and beyond. Andrew, I've heard people talk about that they feel like the depth on the Eagles O line is better this year than it was last year. Do you agree with that sentiment? I do. And really what it what it stems from is and I'm going to I'm going to be transparent. Howie Roseman said this at the podium that that was one of the areas that he was a little concerned about going into training camp, but then you leave training camp and you feel pretty confident in that young group. offensive line coach Chris Cooper deserves a lot of credit to this point for developing that group. And I think the biggest indication of of his sort of handprints in in his uh in terms of development is the summer that Drew Kendall had as a secondyear player. He added weight to his frame. He's 305 pounds right now. He's a center by trade, but I thought he did some good things at guard, a lot stronger at the point of attack. Then you have Willie Lampin, who did not practice for the Eagles last year. Remember, he was on injured reserve, so this was our first look at him in practice. And he did a nice job. He emerged very quickly from the third team. And he too was viewed as a center guard and got reps there. Michael Morris, a young player. Markeel Bell, another young player. And and so you look at all of these guys and it's easy to become enamored with what they have uh not only for the here and now, but also potentially for the future. So, I feel really uh really confident in this group based off what I've seen. Now, they have to go out there and and perform on the field if their number is called, but I think history will show you and that this offensive line, I mean, they're they've they there's been a lot of attrition on that line. And so to expect, you know, the five starters to be to have a clean bill of health all season might be a little bit of a of a pipe dream, but it should be reassuring that the Eagles have some young talent there behind them waiting in the wings. >> And let's look over to defense. What is your perspective right now on the edge rusher situation? Because with Brenard, you know, out until we're not really sure when he's coming back. That's what Vicious said a couple weeks ago and it seems to be the case still. You know, we know Jelix Hunt. We know what he is. We've heard good things about Nolan Smith coming out of camp, but it feels like kind of like last year where it's like they're thin at a position that you maybe you weren't expecting them to be so thin at. >> I I don't view them as being thin there actually. In fact, I know Vic Fangio mentioned that offball linebacker ILB as he calls them is probably the deepest position on defense. I would counter that and and maybe, you know, look at edge rusher as one of those positions because if there were a a position group that could withstand if Jonathan Grard isn't going to be available for week one or week two, it would be that edge rusher room because of the the progression of a Jix Hunt. I thought Nolan Smith, while he doesn't get talked about a lot, really showcased his physicality, some juice as a pass rusher, most importantly he's healthy right now. he should benefit from more snaps. Jayl Hunt, I think, is primed for a breakout season. He made a play every practice. And then you have players beyond them that are experienced veterans in AK EAD. You have AJ Epanessa who is being asked to do different things in this system that he hasn't had to do at any other point in Buffalo. But I think that he's progressed nicely. And you have other players, you know, beyond that on the practice squad like Keshan James Newbie. The point that I'm driving home here is that they are well stocked at this position. Each player brings something different to the table. And when Jonathan Grard does return, I'm not expecting him to all of a sudden take on 55 60 snaps. He hasn't practiced at all with the Eagles. He hasn't practiced at all since December. He had the shoulder injury with the Vikings. So, they may have to slowplay that a little bit and gradually build him up throughout the year. You also have to wonder where he is in terms of just a physical strength perspective because he hasn't been able to lift weights with that pec strain, I would imagine. And so I I I think all things taken into account here, the Eagles have enough there to navigate the interim if Grard isn't going to be back uh to start the season. >> What do you think the you know when if there's ever a situation where Jillian Carter and Jordan Davis are not on the field? You know, we know about Mororrow AMO. Do you think they're going to try to get a JMO more opportunities this year because of the year he had last year, or do you think he is solidly going to be in the context of a number three DTackle reps? >> I'm smiling as you ask that question because I am bullish and have been bullish on Mororrow JO. One of my favorite players, if not my favorite player to watch on the Eagles defense. Extremely violent. He actually played the most snaps of any Eagles defensive tackle last season. I believe he had 740. It was 66% of the defensive snaps. Now, there's context there. Jaylen Carter missed the the week six game against the Giants with a heel injury. Of course, he missed three down the stretch with the shoulders injury. And, you know, I I think that he is going to continue to to be someone that they lean on. I don't know that he'll take on the same amount of snaps that he had last year, all things equal, if everyone's healthy. But you also have other players behind Mororrow JO as well. Byron Young, I would say, is one of the more underrated and important depth pieces on this team. Someone who Vic Fangio likes, he trusts. He gives you positional versatility. He's a backup nose tackle. And so, there's a lot of trust and confidence in him that if his numbers called, he can step in and give you quality production as well. And then of course the the shining star of the preseason, one of them was Ty Robinson had to say and and what that all means. But I can tell you that watching Ty Robinson really about the second half of training camp after he got into a little bit of a dust out with Tyra Steen, it almost unlocked a confidence in him and it sort of awakened him a little bit. He was playing with a lot more ferocity. I thought that his his hand usage, his violence at the point of attack was a lot more apparent, and that's really what you want to see, but 3 weeks of of production in training camp isn't isn't probably going to be enough to leaprog Byron Young in the pecking order. But it does indicate that he's playable and that he's someone that if he needs to step in, he he's going to give you some quality reps. By the way, Andrew, I wanted to hit on with you the safety position because I feel like there's a lot of and I'm not trying to project anything on anyone, but people who are not from the Inside the Birds podcast, I'll put it that way. Okay. People who are not ITB like you and Jeff and Adam who are maybe putting out some misinformation, shall I call it, about what is going on, who is going to play safety, what are the reps going to look like, what is that position going to look like this year. Well, Drew Makuba is going to take the top spot there and handle that Reed Blankenshipesque role. Communication is going to be paramount with him. He's a a young player that started 10 games last year, but I really like the way that he acquitted himself this summer. He didn't necessarily come up with any interceptions, but it's about limiting mistakes, communicating, and being where you need to be. being fundamentally sound and assignment sound is critical aspects of what Vic Fangio asks of his safeties. So I I feel pretty confident in Makuba. Marcus Eps is a steady veteran. There's a lot of trust there. He had a really quiet summer, but that's not always indicative of whether a player had a good or a bad summer, but he's not a ball hawking safety, but he is someone who's going to handle the the communication, be essentially a traffic cop back there. He's taken the lion share of the reps when the Eagles are in nickel opposite Makuba and I I think that he brings you a physical element there at safety. Michael Carter II is a player that I was really impressed with going into training camp. I thought that he was going to emerge as the starter. It just gives you a lot more optionality, the ability to be multiple on defense. And really when you look at the way the NFL defenses are trending this modern era, you're seeing more players of the build of a Makuba or a Michael Carter. And I like his his movement ability, his eye discipline. He had three interceptions in training camp, led the Eagles there, and found himself around the football quite a bit. But I think Josh, his versatility almost works against him here because he wears three different hats. Nickelback, safety, and he's the Eagles dime defensive back as well. So he might be too valuable, and you if you're Vic Vanji, you want to have him on standby so you can deploy him wherever um wherever is needed. So I think they have a solid three there. And then let's not forget Cooper Deene repping there in base when the Eagles are in base. So I think they have a decent amount of of talent there. Different types of skill sets. And I also want to say that it is a shame that uh Andre Sam injured himself in the preseason finale. He was lighting it up. This is a guy Josh who >> for two summers he found himself on the outside looking in. I thought last summer was going to be the year that he was able to latch on, but then definitely this year, the way he was playing and the reps that he was getting in training camp, it's very clear that Vic Vanio, Joe Casper, they really like him. I thought that he might have been able to elbow his way into the roster conversation and then he suffers an injury and is not able to leave on his own terms. That was a shame to see, but that that's the sort of the synopsis there of what I've observed from the safety room from 17 practices. >> Of course, again, this is the initial 53. There could be more changes. We still got several days to go before Eagles versus Commanders week 1. Of course, you hear that game right here on 973 ESPN. For more Eagles coverage and analysis, check out the Insidethebirds podcast. Like, subscribe, and download wherever you get your podcasts, insidethebirds.com. Catch all of Andrew's writing coverage. And don't forget to follow him on the Xplatform at Andrew Deeco. Andrew, great stuff today. Enjoy the weekend. is the it's your final weekend without the Eagles. You have college football, but you could relax a little bit for that, right? There's always work to be done, Josh. There's always work to be done. But I appreciate you, man. Take care.
